properties.summary: A compact 4.2-acre project that reportedly already has city approval for 43 RV sites, installed water and inspected 30A/50A electrical infrastructure, plus an unfinished common/wash-house building. The acreage is tight, but the entitlement and utility head start plus advertised owner financing could eliminate a large portion of JOE VISION Phase 1 cost and risk. The decisive questions are whether the 43-site approvals are current and transferable, whether the layout is operationally comfortable for large rigs, and what it really costs to finish sewer and open legally.

confirmed: Current listing marketing asks $375,000 for approximately 4.2 acres.
The property is marketed as approved/permitted for 43 RV sites.
Listing marketing reports water installed at the sites and 30A/50A electrical hookups installed, inspected and signed off.
Four electrical meters and an unfinished approximately 600-700 sq. ft. common/wash-house building are reported.
Sewer engineering/plans are reported approved, with seller-estimated completion cost around $60,000.
unknowns: Are all 43 RV-site approvals, permits and utility inspections current, transferable and sufficient to open after completion?
What are the exact owner-financing terms: down payment, rate, amortization, balloon, personal guarantee and prepayment provisions?
Does the 4.2-acre layout provide acceptable pad dimensions, internal roads, turning radii, setbacks, parking, fire access and guest privacy for 43 modern RVs?
What is the contractor-backed cost to complete the municipal sewer connection, site laterals, restroom/laundry building and remaining civil work?
What stormwater, drainage, landscaping, lighting, signage, ADA and fire-marshal work remains?
Is there sufficient electrical and water capacity for full 43-site occupancy under peak conditions?
What local nightly/monthly demand and achievable rates support the completed project?
dealKillers: The advertised 43-site approval is expired, non-transferable, conditional on major additional work or materially different from the current site plan.
The compact layout cannot safely or comfortably accommodate the target RV mix and required circulation.
Sewer, drainage, civil, fire-code or utility completion costs push total project basis beyond a defensible operating value.
Owner-financing terms are too aggressive to preserve working capital during buildout and lease-up.
Flood or drainage conditions create unacceptable operating or construction risk.
nextActions: Obtain the stamped 43-site plan, city approvals, permits, inspection sign-offs and written confirmation from Brewton that approvals remain valid and transfer with the property.
Request written owner-financing terms before spending money on deeper diligence.
Get contractor pricing for the complete sewer connection and all remaining work required for certificate of occupancy/opening.
Overlay the approved plan with large-rig turning templates, pad dimensions, fire access, guest parking and amenity space to test whether 43 sites is operationally realistic.
Verify floodplain, drainage, parcel boundaries, title, access and utility capacities.
Build a conservative 30-, 36- and 43-site operating model rather than assuming every approved pad should be built.
